goal: Bound the A-v1 daily utility from above with one-sided relaxations and pair the bound with the recorded control arms, to decide how much headroom exists above the strongest admissible non-learning control.
why: the only reference used so far ("clairvoyant") is a greedy value/energy heuristic that the strongest rule beats (uncond_dynamic 1161.7 > clairvoyant 1151.6 in the earlier panel), so it is not an upper bound and the headroom question is still open
scope_boundary: Analysis only: no arm is run, no policy is trained, no model is loaded, no new data is generated. Every relaxation is one-sided so the number produced is an upper bound, and the recorded control arms are used as a falsification oracle for each relaxation.

objective.utility: revenue - fuel - reject_loss, with fuel = 0.1 * distance_km >= 0 and reject_loss = 0 at p_c=0
objective.bound_chain: utility <= revenue; revenue = sum of per-class constants; so a revenue upper bound bounds utility

relaxations.R1_servability: earliest possible service start is max(straight-line travel time, reveal_time); straight-line distance is a lower bound on any real travel distance, so an order whose earliest service cannot finish inside its time window is unservable by any policy
relaxations.R2_energy: serving an order necessarily charges at least its pre-cooling energy q*0.15*(25-target_c) plus a non-negative door term, so the served set obeys sum(e_lower) <= B
relaxations.R3_vehicle_time: serving an order consumes at least one out-and-back trip plus the loading service time, so the served set obeys sum(tau) <= num_vehicles * horizon
relaxations.aggregation: fractional knapsack on R2, on R3, and their minimum; each is an upper bound on the 0/1 knapsack

variants.tw_and_horizon: time window plus return inside the booking horizon

relaxations.variant_caveat: tw_and_horizon is tighter and therefore riskier; the recorded arms decide whether it is admissible, because an arm-day that serves an order outside that set falsifies it

falsification_oracle: revenue <= reachable revenue on every arm-day
accumulated vehicle time within num_vehicles*horizon on every arm-day
known_boundary: the recorded control rows come from a batch whose run_a1_step2_gate.py and scenario_saa.py differ from the current files; this stage deliberately depends only on unchanged modules and rebuilds the contract directly, and it verifies both the contract hash and the dataset hash against the recorded identity before using the rows
